1.title: 〜ように 言う / 頼む / 注意する
1.structure: Verb (Dictionary / ない form) + ように + 言う/頼む/注意する
1.explanation: Used to indirectly quote a command, request, or piece of advice given by someone. It transforms direct commands into reported speech.

examples.jp: 先生に宿題を忘れないように言われました。
examples.en: I was told by the teacher not to forget my homework.

examples.jp: 医者にタバコを吸わないように注意されました。
examples.en: I was warned by the doctor not to smoke.

1.summary: Reports someone else's command, request, or advice indirectly — the ように clause carries the content of what was said, without quoting their exact words.
1.details:
### 〜ように 言う／頼む／注意する: Reporting Commands Indirectly

| Verb | Nuance |
| :--- | :--- |
| 〜ように**言う** | Neutral — "told to..." |
| 〜ように**頼む** | A request — "asked to..." |
| 〜ように**注意する** | A warning — "warned to..." |

先生に宿題を忘れない**ように**言われました。 *(I was told by the teacher not to forget my homework.)*
医者にタバコを吸わない**ように**注意されました。 *(I was warned by the doctor not to smoke.)*

Because ように always attaches to a dictionary form or ない-form (not a direct quote), it works for both requests to *do* something and requests *not* to do something — unlike direct quotation with と言われました, which would need to quote the exact words used (「宿題を忘れるな」と言われました).

5.title: 〜ばいい / 〜たらいい / 〜といい
5.structure: Verb (Conditional ば / たら / と) + いい
5.explanation: Used in questions to ask for advice. Used in statements to give advice ('You should...'). Can also express a hope or wish for the future.

examples.jp: どこでカメラを買ったらいいですか。
examples.en: Where should I buy a camera? (Asking for advice)

examples.jp: 明日、晴れるといいですね。
examples.en: I hope it will be sunny tomorrow. (Wish/Hope)

5.summary: ばいい／たらいい／といい all mean roughly 'it would be good if...' — used in questions to ask for advice, and in statements to give advice or express a hope.
5.details:
どこでカメラを買っ**たらいいですか**。 *(Where should I buy a camera? — asking for advice.)*
明日、晴れる**といいですね**。 *(I hope it'll be sunny tomorrow. — a wish.)*

All three conditional forms (ば／たら／と) can combine with いい here, largely interchangeably in casual speech — see N4 Lessons 1 and 10 for the fuller comparison of these three conditionals in other contexts. と＋いい specifically leans toward expressing a hope about something outside the speaker's control (weather, luck), while ば/たらいい more often ask for or give practical advice.

5.title: 〜おかげで / 〜せいで
5.structure: Verb/Adj (Plain) / Noun + の + おかげで / せいで
5.explanation: '〜おかげで' is used for positive outcomes resulting from someone or something (Thanks to). '〜せいで' is used for negative outcomes, blaming the cause (Because of / Thanks to ~).

examples.jp: 先生のおかげで、試験に合格しました。
examples.en: Thanks to the teacher, I passed the exam.

examples.jp: バスが遅れたせいで、授業に遅刻しました。
examples.en: Because the bus was late, I was late for class.

5.summary: おかげで attributes a favorable outcome to its cause ('thanks to'); せいで attributes an unfavorable outcome, assigning blame ('because of,' in a negative sense).
5.details:
### おかげで (Positive) vs せいで (Negative)

| Pattern | Outcome | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **〜おかげで** | Favorable | 先生の**おかげで**、試験に合格しました。 *(Thanks to the teacher, I passed the exam.)* |
| **〜せいで** | Unfavorable, assigns blame | バスが遅れた**せいで**、授業に遅刻しました。 *(Because the bus was late, I was late for class.)* |

The sentence-final versions work the same way: 先生のおかげだ ("it's thanks to my teacher") and バスのせいだ ("it's the bus's fault") — せいだ is a more pointed way of assigning blame than せいで mid-sentence. Because せいで inherently blames a cause, it can sound accusatory if used about a person directly (あなたのせいで...) — worth being mindful of tone.

6.title: N は 〜の 一つだ
6.structure: Noun は [Category/Group] の 一つだ
6.explanation: Used to state that the subject (Noun) belongs to a larger group or is one instance among many. Very common in essays and formal writing.

examples.jp: 漢字は、日本語の文字の一つです。
examples.en: Kanji is one of the writing systems in Japanese.

examples.jp: この町は、日本で最も美しい場所の一つだ。
examples.en: This town is one of the most beautiful places in Japan.

6.summary: Nは〜の一つだ states that N belongs to a larger category or is one example among several — a common phrase in essays, formal writing, and descriptive statements.
6.details:
漢字は、日本語の文字**の一つです**。 *(Kanji is one of the writing systems in Japanese.)*
この町は、日本で最も美しい場所**の一つだ**。 *(This town is one of the most beautiful places in Japan.)*

Almost always paired with a superlative or defining category phrase (最も〜, 主な〜, 代表的な〜) right before の一つ — the pattern is really saying "out of [category], this is one member," which is why it reads naturally in formal/essay contexts introducing or classifying a topic.

6.title: N にとって
6.meaning: For N / To N (From the standpoint of)
6.explanation: Expresses a perspective or standpoint. It means 'as far as Noun is concerned' or 'to Noun'. It is often followed by an adjective indicating value, importance, or difficulty.

examples.jp: 私にとって、家族は一番大切なものです。
examples.en: To me, family is the most important thing.

examples.jp: 外国人にとって、日本の習慣を理解するのは難しい。
examples.en: For foreigners, understanding Japanese customs is difficult.

6.summary: にとって marks a standpoint — 'as far as N is concerned' or 'to N' — almost always followed by an adjective judging value, importance, or difficulty.
6.details:
私**にとって**、家族は一番大切なものです。 *(To me, family is the most important thing.)*
外国人**にとって**、日本の習慣を理解するのは難しい。 *(For foreigners, understanding Japanese customs is difficult.)*

> **Common mistake**: にとって marks a *judging perspective*, not a direct recipient of an action — you can't use it where に alone (or への, のために) would be needed for a literal recipient. Compare 私にとって大切だ (important, from my perspective) with 私にプレゼントをくれた (gave a present to me, a literal recipient) — these use two entirely different にs.

6.title: N の 代わりに
6.meaning: Instead of N / On behalf of N
6.structure: Noun + の + 代わりに (かわりに)
6.explanation: Indicates substitution. It can mean doing something in place of an object (using X instead of Y) or on behalf of a person.

examples.jp: コーヒーの代わりに、お茶を飲みます。
examples.en: I will drink tea instead of coffee.

examples.jp: 社長の代わりに、私が会議に出席します。
examples.en: I will attend the meeting on behalf of the company president.

6.summary: の代わりに expresses substitution — either using one thing in place of another, or acting on someone's behalf.
6.details:
### Two Uses of の代わりに

| Use | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Substituting one object for another** | コーヒー**の代わりに**、お茶を飲みます。 *(I'll drink tea instead of coffee.)* |
| **Acting on someone's behalf** | 社長**の代わりに**、私が会議に出席します。 *(I will attend the meeting on the president's behalf.)* |

代わりに literally means "in place of" — context (an object vs. a person) determines whether the natural English gloss is "instead of" or "on behalf of," but the underlying logic (substitution) is identical in both cases.

7.title: 〜から〜にかけて
7.structure: Noun 1 (Time/Place) + から + Noun 2 (Time/Place) + にかけて
7.explanation: Indicates a rough span of time or space. Unlike '〜から〜まで' which has clear start and end points, '〜にかけて' implies a continuous or intermittent action/state spread over that general period or area.

examples.jp: 明日は、昼から夕方にかけて雨が降るでしょう。
examples.en: Tomorrow, it will likely rain from noon through the late afternoon.

examples.jp: 関東地方から東北地方にかけて、大きな地震がありました。
examples.en: There was a large earthquake spanning from the Kanto region through the Tohoku region.

7.summary: 〜から〜にかけて covers a rough, continuous or intermittent span of time/space — unlike 〜から〜まで, which marks clear, definite start and end points.
7.details:
### にかけて vs まで

| Pattern | Boundaries | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **〜から〜にかけて** (here) | Rough, approximate span; action may be continuous or intermittent throughout | 昼から夕方**にかけて**雨が降るでしょう。 *(It'll rain sometime between noon and evening.)* |
| 〜から〜まで | Clear, definite start/end | 9時から5時**まで**働きます。 *(I work from 9 to 5 — precise hours.)* |

にかけて is common in weather forecasts and news reports about earthquakes, disasters, or seasonal changes — situations where the exact boundary isn't the point, just the general area/period affected.

8.title: 〜によって / 〜による
8.meaning: Depending on / By means of / Due to
8.structure: Noun + によって / Noun + による + Noun
8.explanation: A versatile grammar point. It can mean 'depending on the noun' (variation), 'by means of' (method), 'caused by' (cause), or 'created by' (passive actor).

examples.jp: 国によって、文化や習慣が違います。
examples.en: Culture and customs differ depending on the country.

examples.jp: この絵はピカソによって描かれました。
examples.en: This painting was drawn by Picasso.

examples.jp: 台風によって、木が倒れました。
examples.en: The tree fell due to the typhoon.

8.summary: A highly versatile pattern: によって can mean 'depending on' (variation), 'by means of' (method), or 'caused by/done by' (the agent of a passive sentence) — context decides which sense applies.
8.details:
### The Three Senses of によって

| Sense | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Variation** ("depending on") | 国**によって**、文化や習慣が違います。 *(Culture differs depending on the country.)* |
| **Passive agent** ("by [creator]") | この絵はピカソ**によって**描かれました。 *(This painting was drawn by Picasso.)* |
| **Cause** ("due to/because of") | 台風**によって**、木が倒れました。 *(The tree fell due to the typhoon.)* |

See N4 Lesson 12-5's によって marking the "creator" specifically in passive sentences about invention/creation/discovery — this is the umbrella pattern, and that point zooms in on one sense of it.

8.title: 〜に対して
8.structure: Noun + に対して (たいして)
8.explanation: Used to indicate an attitude or action directed 'towards' someone or something. It can also be used to show a clear contrast between two things ('In contrast to A, B is...').

examples.jp: 先生に対して、そんな言葉を使ってはいけません。
examples.en: You must not use such words towards a teacher.

examples.jp: 兄が静かなのに対して、弟はとても元気だ。
examples.en: In contrast to my older brother being quiet, my younger brother is very energetic.

8.summary: に対して marks an attitude or action directed toward someone/something, and can also frame an explicit contrast between two things.
8.details:
### The Two Uses of に対して

| Use | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Directed toward** (an attitude/action aimed at someone) | 先生**に対して**、そんな言葉を使ってはいけません。 *(You must not use such words towards a teacher.)* |
| **Contrast** ("in contrast to...") | 兄が静かなの**に対して**、弟はとても元気だ。 *(In contrast to my quiet older brother, my younger brother is very energetic.)* |

The "directed toward" sense often carries a slightly formal, sometimes confrontational nuance (an attitude, opinion, or demand aimed squarely at someone) — compare with にとって (Lesson 6-2), which instead marks a standpoint/perspective rather than a directed action.

9.title: 〜ば〜ほど
9.explanation: Used to express that as one condition changes, another condition changes proportionally. You repeat the same verb or adjective twice (once in 'ba' form, once in dictionary form).

examples.jp: 日本語は、話せば話すほど上手になります。
examples.en: The more you speak Japanese, the better you become.

examples.jp: スーパーは家から近ければ近いほど便利です。
examples.en: The closer the supermarket is to home, the more convenient it is.

9.summary: ばほど repeats the same verb or adjective in both the ば-conditional and dictionary-form halves to show that a degree scales up (or down) together — 'the more..., the more...'
9.details:
日本語は、**話せば話すほど**上手になります。 *(The more you speak Japanese, the better you become.)*
スーパーは家から**近ければ近いほど**便利です。 *(The closer the supermarket is, the more convenient.)*

This is the same 〜ば〜ほど pattern covered in N4 Lesson 10-6 — the same verb/adjective must appear on both sides, once conditionalized with ば, once left in dictionary/plain form and followed by ほど.

9.title: 〜ばかり / 〜てばかりいる
9.structure: Noun + ばかり / Verb (て form) + ばかりいる
9.explanation: Used to emphasize that there is an unusually large amount of one thing, or that someone is doing only one action repeatedly, usually with a slightly negative connotation.

examples.jp: 休みの日は、ゲームをしてばかりいます。
examples.en: On my days off, I do nothing but play games.

examples.jp: 私の息子は肉ばかり食べて、野菜を食べません。
examples.en: My son eats only meat and won't eat vegetables.

9.summary: ばかり marks an unusually large, exclusive amount of one thing; てばかりいる marks someone doing nothing but one repeated action — both usually carry a mildly critical or exasperated tone.
9.details:
### ばかり (Noun) vs てばかりいる (Verb)

| Form | Attaches to | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **N ＋ ばかり** | A noun | 息子は肉**ばかり**食べて、野菜を食べません。 *(My son eats only meat, won't eat vegetables.)* |
| **Vて-form ＋ ばかりいる** | A repeated action | 休みの日は、ゲームをし**てばかりいます**。 *(On my days off, I do nothing but play games.)* |

Both versions carry an implicit "...and that's a bit much / that's not good" undertone — they're rarely neutral statements of fact, and would sound odd praising something (avoid using this to mean 彼はいつも勉強していて偉い, a compliment; だけ or いつも would be more neutral choices there).

9.title: 〜について
9.structure: Noun + について / Noun + についての + Noun
9.explanation: Indicates the topic or subject of an action, thought, or research. Similar to 'about' or 'concerning' in English.

examples.jp: 日本の歴史について調べています。
examples.en: I am researching about Japanese history.

examples.jp: 環境問題についてのスピーチを聞きました。
examples.en: I listened to a speech regarding environmental issues.

9.summary: について marks the topic of an action, thought, or piece of research — 'about' or 'concerning' — with についての available to modify a following noun directly.
9.details:
日本の歴史**について**調べています。 *(I am researching Japanese history.)*
環境問題**についての**スピーチを聞きました。 *(I listened to a speech about environmental issues.)*

について is one of the most common, neutral ways to introduce a topic — see Lesson 15-2's に関する／に関して for a more formal written equivalent of the same meaning, typically found in academic writing, official notices, and news reports rather than everyday conversation.

10.title: 〜ずに
10.structure: Verb (ない form, drop ない) + ずに (※する -> せずに)
10.explanation: A written or slightly formal equivalent of '〜ないで'. It means doing an action without doing another expected action.

examples.jp: 朝ごはんを食べずに学校へ行きました。
examples.en: I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.jp: 辞書を使わずに、新聞を読みました。
examples.en: I read the newspaper without using a dictionary.

10.summary: ずに is a written/formal equivalent of ないで, describing doing one action without doing another expected one.
10.details:
朝ごはんを食べ**ずに**学校へ行きました。 *(I went to school without eating breakfast.)*
辞書を使わ**ずに**、新聞を読みました。 *(I read the newspaper without using a dictionary.)*

Formed from the ない-form by dropping ない and adding ずに (する is irregular: せずに, not しずに). The trailing に is optional (ず［に］) — both shapes mean exactly the same thing, and either is acceptable in writing.

12.title: 〜（ら）れる (Indirect Passive)
12.explanation: In addition to direct passive sentences, this form is used when the speaker is adversely affected by an action, often an action involving an intransitive verb (like raining or crying).

examples.jp: 雨に降られて、服がぬれてしまった。
examples.en: I was caught in the rain (adversely affected by the rain falling), and my clothes got wet.

examples.jp: 夜中に隣の赤ちゃんに泣かれて、眠れませんでした。
examples.en: The baby next door cried in the middle of the night, and I couldn't sleep.

12.summary: Beyond the direct passive, this れる／られる form describes the speaker being adversely affected by someone else's action — including intransitive verbs like raining or crying, which have no direct object of their own to become the passive subject.
12.details:
### The "Suffering/Adversity" Indirect Passive

雨に**降られて**、服がぬれてしまった。 *(I was caught in the rain, and my clothes got wet.)*
夜中に隣の赤ちゃんに**泣かれて**、眠れませんでした。 *(The baby next door cried, and I couldn't sleep.)*

This mirrors the "suffering passive" you may have seen in N4 Lesson 12-3 (わたしは弟にパソコンを壊されました) — but here it extends even to intransitive verbs (降る, 泣く) that have no direct object at all. The speaker (implicit or は-marked) is simply inconvenienced by someone/something else's action, even though grammatically that action doesn't act "on" them directly.

12.title: 〜っぱなし
12.meaning: Leaving something as it is (Negative connotation)
12.structure: Verb (ます stem) + っぱなし
12.explanation: Indicates leaving something in a certain state, usually when it should be changed or put away. Often has a negative connotation.

examples.jp: 服が脱ぎっぱなしだ。かたづけないから、部屋がきたない。
examples.en: You just take your clothes off and leave them lying around. You don't put them away, so your room is untidy.

examples.jp: こらっ。ドアが開けっぱなしだよ。早く閉めなさい。
examples.en: Hey, you've left the door open. Hurry up and shut it.

12.summary: っぱなし describes leaving something in a state it shouldn't be left in — usually implying carelessness or a mild scolding.
12.details:
服が脱ぎ**っぱなし**だ。かたづけないから、部屋がきたない。
*(You leave your clothes lying around. You don't put them away, so your room is messy.)*
ドアが開け**っぱなし**だよ。早く閉めなさい。
*(You've left the door open. Hurry up and close it.)*

っぱなし attaches to a ます-stem (脱ぎ, 開け) and always carries that "left as-is, and that's a problem" nuance — compare with the more neutral V-たまま (N4 Lesson 9-5), which can describe a persisting state without necessarily implying it's wrong or careless.

13.title: 〜たて
13.explanation: Indicates that an action has just been completed, emphasizing freshness or newness. Often used with food or products.

examples.jp: 焼きたてのパンはおいしいです。
examples.en: Freshly baked bread is delicious.

examples.jp: ペンキ塗立て。
examples.en: Freshly painted. (Sign)

13.summary: たて marks that something has just been made or completed, emphasizing its freshness — most common with food and freshly finished products.
13.details:
焼き**たて**のパンはおいしいです。 *(Freshly baked bread is delicious.)*
ペンキ塗り**たて**。 *(Freshly painted — a warning sign.)*

たて attaches directly to a verb's ます-stem (焼き, 塗り) and always highlights that not much time has passed since completion — similar in spirit to N4 Lesson 21-2's ばかりです, but たて is used specifically as a noun-modifier (焼きたてのパン) rather than a sentence-ending predicate, and leans toward food/products rather than general events.

13.title: たとえ〜ても
13.explanation: Used to present a hypothetical situation and state that the outcome or conclusion will not change regardless of that situation.

examples.jp: たとえ雨が降っても、試合は行われます。
examples.en: Even if it rains, the match will be held.

examples.jp: たとえ親が反対しても、私は彼と結婚します。
examples.en: Even if my parents oppose it, I will marry him.

13.summary: たとえ〜ても sets up a hypothetical, even extreme, situation and insists the outcome won't change regardless — 'even if X happens, Y still holds.'
13.details:
たとえ雨が降っ**ても**、試合は行われます。 *(Even if it rains, the match will be held.)*
たとえ親が反対し**ても**、私は彼と結婚します。 *(Even if my parents oppose it, I will marry him.)*

たとえ at the front of the sentence isn't strictly required grammatically (ても alone can express "even if"), but adding it emphasizes the hypothetical, no-matter-what nature of the condition — it signals from the very start of the sentence that whatever follows won't change the outcome.

13.title: 〜たりしない
13.explanation: A strong denial of doing a certain action or things like it.

examples.jp: 私は絶対にうそをついたりしません。
examples.en: I absolutely do not do things like tell lies.

examples.jp: あんなひどいことを言ったりしないでください。
examples.en: Please don't do things like say such terrible things.

13.summary: たりしない is a strong, blanket denial that the speaker would ever do a certain action (or similar actions) — an emphatic negative built on the 〜たり listing pattern.
13.details:
私は絶対にうそをつい**たりしません**。 *(I absolutely do not do things like tell lies.)*
あんなひどいことを言っ**たりしないで**ください。 *(Please don't do things like say such terrible things.)*

Built on the same たり listing pattern as N5 Lesson 19-3, but negated (たりしない rather than たりする) — this frames the denied action as one example of a whole category of unacceptable behavior, giving the denial extra emphatic force compared to a plain negative (うそをつきません).

13.title: 〜ほど
13.meaning: To the extent that ~ / So ~ that ~
13.explanation: Expresses the degree or extent of a state or action by comparing it to an extreme example.

examples.jp: 死ぬほど疲れました。
examples.en: I am tired to the extent of dying (dead tired).

examples.jp: 涙が出るほど笑いました。
examples.en: I laughed so much that tears came out.

13.summary: ほど expresses degree by pointing to an extreme, vivid example — 'to the extent that...' or 'so much that...'
13.details:
死ぬ**ほど**疲れました。 *(I'm tired to the point of dying — dead tired.)*
涙が出る**ほど**笑いました。 *(I laughed so much that tears came out.)*

ほど here attaches to a full clause describing an extreme outcome (死ぬ, 涙が出る) as a colorful, exaggerated way of measuring the true degree of the preceding statement — this hyperbolic style is common in casual speech for emphasis. See N4 Lesson 10-6 and Lesson 9-1 for ほど's other major use, in the 〜ば〜ほど "the more... the more..." pattern — a related but distinct grammatical role for the same word.

14.title: 〜際（に）
14.structure: Verb (Dictionary/た-form) / Noun の + 際（に）
14.explanation: Means more or less the same as '〜とき', but is used mainly in formal writing or public announcements.

examples.jp: 外出の際、必ずフロントに鍵をお預けください。
examples.en: When leaving the hotel, please be sure to leave your key at the front desk.

examples.jp: PCをお使いの場合は、チェックインの際、必ずお申し出ください。
examples.en: If you are going to use a PC, please be sure to say so when you check in.

14.summary: 際（に）means roughly the same as とき, but is reserved for formal writing, public announcements, and business contexts.
14.details:
外出の**際**、必ずフロントに鍵をお預けください。 *(When leaving the hotel, please be sure to leave your key at the front desk.)*
PCをお使いの場合は、チェックインの**際**、必ずお申し出ください。 *(If using a PC, please mention it at check-in.)*

Swap とき for 際 whenever the register shifts formal — hotel notices, workplace instructions, ceremonial speeches — but not in everyday conversation, where とき remains completely natural and 際 would sound stiff.

15.title: 〜たびに
15.structure: Verb (Dictionary form) / Noun の + たびに

examples.jp: 隣の家のお嬢さんは会うたびにきれいになっている。
examples.en: The girl next door gets prettier every time I see her.

examples.jp: 欧米では転職するたびに給料が上がるというが、日本では必ずしもそうではない。
examples.en: They say that in Western countries, one's salary rises every time one changes jobs, but this is not necessarily so in Japan.

15.summary: たびに means 'every time' — a recurring event triggers the same result each time it happens.
15.details:
隣の家のお嬢さんは会う**たびに**きれいになっている。 *(The girl next door gets prettier every time I see her.)*

たびに attaches to a verb's dictionary form or Nの (帰省のたびに, "every time I go home") and always implies repetition — each individual occurrence of the first event brings about the same observation or result in the second clause.

15.title: 〜に関する／関して
15.explanation: Indicates what is contained in the noun. Means more or less the same as '〜について', but is more of a written expression.

examples.jp: 今回の講演会に関してご意見のある方はこの紙に書いて出口の箱にお入れください。
examples.en: Would anyone who has any comments or suggestions about this lecture please write them on these slips of paper and place them in the box at the exit.

examples.jp: 東京で環境問題に関する会議が開かれた。
examples.en: A conference on environmental issues was held in Tokyo.

15.summary: に関する／に関して mean roughly the same as について, but are more formal, written expressions typically found in official or academic contexts.
15.details:
東京で環境問題**に関する**会議が開かれた。 *(A conference on environmental issues was held in Tokyo.)*

| Form | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| **に関して** | Attaches mid-sentence, like について | 講演会に関してご意見のある方は... |
| **に関する** | Modifies a following noun directly | 環境問題に関する会議 |

See Lesson 9-3's について for the more casual/neutral everyday equivalent of this same meaning — に関する／に関して is the register you'd reach for in a formal announcement, report, or academic paper.

15.title: …わけではない
15.meaning: It doesn't mean that... / It is not necessarily the case that...
15.structure: Verb/Adj (Plain form) / Noun な + わけではない
15.explanation: Negates a conclusion that could easily or generally be drawn from the context or from the situation described.

examples.jp: この店は人気があるが、必ずしも毎日大勢の客が入るわけではない。
examples.en: This shop is popular, but that doesn't mean that huge numbers of customers visit it every day.

examples.jp: 宿題はたくさんあるが、今日中に全部しなければならないわけではない。
examples.en: I've got a lot of homework, but it doesn't mean I have to do it all today.

15.summary: わけではない denies a conclusion that would otherwise seem to follow naturally from what was just said — 'that doesn't mean...' or 'it's not necessarily the case that...'
15.details:
この店は人気があるが、必ずしも毎日大勢の客が入る**わけではない**。
*(This shop is popular, but that doesn't mean huge numbers of customers visit every day.)*

わけではない is almost always paired with が (a contrasting first clause) and often with 必ずしも ("not necessarily") to soften an otherwise-expected conclusion — it's a partial denial, not a full negation: the shop being popular is still true, it's just that one particular inference from that fact doesn't automatically follow.

16.title: 〜ところだった
16.meaning: Was just about to / Almost happened
16.structure: Verb (Dictionary form) + ところだった
16.explanation: Used to express that a situation (often negative or dangerous) was just about to happen, but was narrowly avoided.

examples.jp: もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところだった。
examples.en: I was just about to miss the train (but I made it).

examples.jp: あやうく事故を起こすところだった。
examples.en: I almost caused an accident.

16.summary: ところだった says a (usually negative or dangerous) situation was on the verge of happening, but was narrowly avoided.
16.details:
もう少しで電車に乗り遅れる**ところだった**。 *(I was just about to miss the train — but I made it.)*
あやうく事故を起こす**ところだった**。 *(I almost caused an accident.)*

Often paired with adverbs emphasizing how close a call it was — もう少しで ("just a little more and..."), あやうく ("narrowly") — the whole point of the sentence is relief that the bad outcome was avoided at the last moment. Contrast with N4 Lesson 21-1's plain V dictionary form + ところです ("about to..."), which doesn't carry that same narrowly-averted, past-tense nuance.

17.title: 〜にしては
17.structure: Noun / Plain form (なA -だ -> -である / N -だ -> -) + にしては
17.explanation: Indicates that the outcome or degree of something is different from what would normally be expected based on the given premise (X).

examples.jp: 彼女のピアノの腕は素人にしては相当のものだ。
examples.en: Her piano playing is quite good, considering she is an amateur.

examples.jp: このレポートは一晩で書いたにしてはよくできている。
examples.en: This report is well written, considering it was done in one night.

17.summary: にしては flags that an outcome differs from what you'd normally expect, given the stated premise — 'considering X, Y is surprising.'
17.details:
彼女のピアノの腕は素人**にしては**相当のものだ。 *(Her piano playing is quite good, considering she's an amateur.)*
このレポートは一晩で書いた**にしては**よくできている。 *(This report is well done, considering it was written in one night.)*

にしては always implies a positive or negative surprise relative to expectations set by the premise — "given X, you'd expect Y, but actually Z" — X sets a baseline expectation, and what follows either exceeds or falls short of it.

18.title: 〜に違いない
18.structure: Verb/Adj/Noun (Plain form) + に違いない (※Na-Adj/Noun drop だ)
18.explanation: Expresses the speaker's strong conviction, certainty, or educated guess about a situation. Stronger than '〜はずだ'.

examples.jp: 毎日遅くまで練習しているから、彼は疲れているに違いない。
examples.en: Since he practices late every day, he must undoubtedly be tired.

examples.jp: 犯人はあの男に違いない。
examples.en: The culprit must be that man.

18.summary: に違いない expresses a strong conviction or confident guess — stronger in certainty than はずだ, closer to 'must be' than 'should be.'
18.details:
毎日遅くまで練習しているから、彼は疲れている**に違いない**。
*(Since he practices late every day, he must be tired.)*
犯人はあの男**に違いない**。 *(The culprit must be that man.)*

See N4 Lesson 21-3's はずだ for a related but weaker expectation. On a certainty scale: に違いない (very confident, near-certain conviction) sits above はずだ (a reasoned, likely expectation), which in turn sits above かもしれない (a mere possibility) — see N4 Lesson 7 for that lower end of the same scale.

18.title: 〜に比べて
18.explanation: Used to compare two or more things, highlighting the differences between them.

examples.jp: 今年の夏は去年に比べて涼しい。
examples.en: This summer is cooler compared to last year.

examples.jp: 田舎は都会に比べて物価が安い。
examples.en: Prices are cheaper in the countryside compared to the city.

18.summary: に比べて sets up a direct comparison between two things, highlighting how they differ.
18.details:
今年の夏は去年**に比べて**涼しい。 *(This summer is cooler compared to last year.)*
田舎は都会**に比べて**物価が安い。 *(Prices are cheaper in the countryside compared to the city.)*

に比べて is a neutral, straightforward comparison marker — compare with より (used in the よりほうが comparative pattern, N5 Lesson 12-3), which structures a comparison around choosing/preferring one option; に比べて simply states how two things differ, without necessarily framing one as better.

19.title: 〜として（は）／〜としても／〜としての
19.meaning: From the viewpoint of / As for / In the capacity of
19.structure: Noun + として（は）／としても／としての + Noun
19.explanation: Indicates the standpoint, capacity, or role of someone or something. 'としては' emphasizes the standpoint. 'としても' means 'also as'. 'としての' modifies a following noun.

examples.jp: 彼は教師としては素晴らしいが、親としてはどうだろうか。
examples.en: As a teacher he is wonderful, but I wonder about him as a parent.

examples.jp: 趣味としても、スポーツは良いものだ。
examples.en: Even as a hobby, sports are a good thing.

examples.jp: 社長としての責任を果たす。
examples.en: I will fulfill my responsibilities as the company president.

19.summary: として branches into three related forms here: としては (emphasizing a standpoint), としても (also/even as), and としての (modifying a following noun).
19.details:
### The として Family

| Form | Role | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **としては** | Emphasizes a specific standpoint | 彼は教師**としては**素晴らしいが、親としてはどうだろうか。 |
| **としても** | Also/even in the capacity of | 趣味**としても**、スポーツは良いものだ。 |
| **としての** | Modifies a following noun | 社長**としての**責任を果たす。 |

All three build on the base として (role/capacity) — としては often sets up an implicit comparison between two roles (as a teacher... vs as a parent...), while としての simply lets として attach before a noun instead of standing at the end of a clause.

19.title: 〜はもちろん／〜はもとより
19.structure: Noun + はもちろん（のこと）／はもとより
19.explanation: Used to state that the first item is obvious, and then to add another, often more surprising or extreme, item to it. 'はもとより' is more formal.

examples.jp: 彼は英語はもちろん、フランス語も話せる。
examples.en: He can speak French, not to mention English.

examples.jp: 結果はもとより、その過程も重要だ。
examples.en: The process is important, let alone the result.

19.summary: はもちろん／はもとより states that the first item is obviously true, then adds a further, often more surprising, item on top of it — 'not to mention X, Y too.'
19.details:
彼は英語**はもちろん**、フランス語も話せる。 *(Not to mention English, he can also speak French.)*
結果**はもとより**、その過程も重要だ。 *(The result goes without saying — the process matters too.)*

The first item (英語, 結果) is treated as an obvious given; the second item, marked with も, is the point actually being emphasized as also true, often more noteworthy. はもとより is the more formal written equivalent of はもちろん — both share the same underlying "needless to say X, and Y as well" logic.

20.title: 〜を通して／〜を通じて
20.structure: Noun + を通して／を通じて (をとおして / をつうじて)
20.explanation: Has two meanings: 1) To do something 'through' an intermediary (a person, experience, medium). 2) A state continuing 'throughout' a period of time.

examples.jp: インターネットを通して、世界中の人と友達になれる。
examples.en: Through the internet, you can become friends with people all over the world.

examples.jp: この地域は一年を通じて暖かい。
examples.en: This region is warm throughout the year.

20.summary: を通して／を通じて covers two related meanings: doing something 'through' an intermediary, and a state persisting 'throughout' a period of time.
20.details:
### Two Meanings of を通して／を通じて

| Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Through an intermediary** (person, medium, experience) | インターネット**を通して**、世界中の人と友達になれる。 |
| **Throughout a period** of time | この地域は一年**を通じて**暖かい。 |

The two forms are largely interchangeable in most contexts, though を通じて leans slightly more toward the "throughout a time period" reading and formal/written register, while を通して is common in both senses in everyday speech.

20.title: 〜とともに
20.structure: Noun / Verb (Dictionary form) + とともに
20.explanation: Has two meanings: 1) Doing something 'together with' someone/something else (similar to と一緒に). 2) As one thing changes, another thing changes 'along with' it.

examples.jp: 家族とともに、海外へ引っ越すことになった。
examples.en: I am going to move overseas together with my family.

examples.jp: 年をとるとともに、体力が落ちてきた。
examples.en: Along with getting older, my physical strength has declined.

20.summary: とともに covers two meanings: doing something together with someone/something, and one change happening alongside another.
20.details:
### Two Meanings of とともに

| Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Together with** (similar to と一緒に) | 家族**とともに**、海外へ引っ越すことになった。 |
| **Along with** (as one thing changes, so does another) | 年をとる**とともに**、体力が落ちてきた。 |

The "together with" meaning is a more formal/written alternative to と一緒に. The "as X changes, Y changes too" meaning parallels N4 Lesson 10-6's 〜ば〜ほど (both track a paired change), though とともに doesn't require repeating the same verb/adjective the way ば〜ほど does.

21.title: 〜もせずに
21.structure: Verb (ます stem) + もせずに
21.explanation: An archaic or formal expression meaning 'not doing something that one would naturally expect to be done.' It emphasizes the lack of an expected action.

examples.jp: 父は具合が悪いのに、医者に行きもせずに仕事を続けている。
examples.en: Even though my father doesn't feel very well, he won't even go to see a doctor but just carries on working.

examples.jp: 彼は上司の許可を得もせずに、新しいプロジェクトを進めた。
examples.en: He went ahead with a new project without even getting permission from his boss.

21.summary: もせずに is a formal/literary way to emphasize that an action one would normally expect simply wasn't done — 'without even doing...'
21.details:
父は具合が悪いのに、医者に行き**もせずに**仕事を続けている。
*(Even though my father doesn't feel well, he won't even go see a doctor, and just keeps working.)*
彼は上司の許可を得**もせずに**、新しいプロジェクトを進めた。
*(He went ahead with a new project without even getting his boss's permission.)*

Formed from ます-stem + も + せずに (せずに being the formal negative of する, see Lesson 10-1's ずに) — the inserted も adds emphasis: "didn't even do the bare minimum you'd expect." This reads as more literary/formal than a plain ないで／ずに negative.

23.title: 〜可能性がある
23.structure: Plain form + 可能性がある
23.explanation: Means 'Pが起きる可能性がある' (there is a possibility that P will occur or is true). Used similarly to English.

examples.jp: あの学生は基礎的な学力があるし、努力家だから、これから大きく伸びる可能性がある。
examples.en: That student has basic academic ability and is a hard worker, so he has the potential to develop greatly in the future.

examples.jp: 携帯電話は非常に便利だが、場所によってはかからなくなる可能性もある。
examples.en: Mobiles are very handy, but it is also possible that they will not work in certain locations.

23.summary: 可能性がある states that there's a possibility something will happen or is true — functioning much like its literal English translation.
23.details:
あの学生は基礎的な学力があるし、努力家だから、これから大きく伸びる**可能性がある**。
*(That student has basic academic ability and is hard-working, so he has the potential to develop greatly.)*
携帯電話は非常に便利だが、場所によってはかからなくなる**可能性もある**。
*(Mobiles are handy, but there's also a possibility they won't work in certain locations.)*

Because 可能性 is a regular noun ("possibility"), this pattern behaves exactly as you'd expect from English — plain form + 可能性がある/もある — and doesn't carry any of the certainty-scale nuance that はずだ, に違いない, or かもしれない do (see Lesson 18-1's comparison of those).

24.title: V-ます ＋ きる
24.explanation: Means '完全に〜する' (do completely) or, with motion verbs, '最初から最後まで〜する' (do from beginning to end).

examples.jp: 彼はマラソンで42.195kmを走りきった。
examples.en: He completed (ran the entire distance) 42.195 km in the marathon.

examples.jp: 山本さんは疲れきった顔で座り込んでいる。
examples.en: Mr. Yamamoto is slumped in a chair looking completely exhausted.

24.summary: ます-stem + きる means doing something completely, or from beginning to end without stopping — often used with verbs of exertion or motion.
24.details:
彼はマラソンで42.195kmを**走りきった**。 *(He ran the entire 42.195 km marathon distance.)*
山本さんは**疲れきった**顔で座り込んでいる。 *(Mr. Yamamoto is slumped in a chair, looking utterly exhausted.)*

きり attaches to the ます-stem and conveys either "did it completely/thoroughly" (走りきる, 使いきる — "used it all up") or, with a state-verb like 疲れる, an intensified "completely/utterly" reading (疲れきった, "utterly exhausted," stronger than just 疲れた). Common with verbs of physical exertion where reaching the natural endpoint of an effort is the whole point.
